utterances.text: The provisions of this decision to establish the staff, pertaining to the tasks of the staff with regard to the planning, directing, and managing or controlling the actions designed to suppress terrorism, were they derogated --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This decision was passed on the 16th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on a moment. We are being asked I think to repeat the question for the interpreter, Mr. Lukic. Sorry about that. Could you ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am on channel 0 so I don't hear the translators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ask the question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me start from the beginning, Mr. Mijatovic. Were the provisions of this decision to establish the staff dated the 16th of June, 1998, regarding the planning, directing, and managing the actions aimed at suppressing terrorism derogated or abolished by another decision?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is precisely why this part of the decision was never implemented, the part that related to the tasks of the staff, because the decision was issued on the 16th of June, 1998, and a plan was adopted, a plan for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija was adopted at the state top and this is one of the main reasons why the staff did not really organize or plan those actions. So the plan was adopted at the highest level of the state. It was -- it had primacy over this decision and that is why this decision was never implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what forces did take part in addition -- in accordance with this decision?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in addition to the MUP forces, the Army of Yugoslavia personnel were also involved in suppressing terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask for Prosecution Exhibit P2166 to be placed on the screen instead of this exhibit. As we can see, this -- these are the minutes of the meeting of the inter-departmental staff for suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. The date is the 2nd of November, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 3, please, on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, could you please read on this page the paragraph that is underlined, it is underlined electronically.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The one that begins: "Pursuant to the decision ..."?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: "Pursuant to the decision adopted at the 5th Session of the Supreme Defence Council on the 9th of June, 1998, the Law on the Yugoslav Army, the Law on Defence, and the Rules of Service of the Yugoslav Army, a plan to suppress terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija was drawn up which provided for the engagement of units of the Serbian MUP and the Yugoslav Army."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can it be seen from this document when a decision was made to draft this plan for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the decision was made on the 9th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to this document, which body made the decision to draw up this plan for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: This body is called the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did anyone from the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia sit on this council?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can we see pursuant to what regulations, what legislation, this decision was made?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, this decision was made pursuant to the Law on the Yugoslav Army, the Law on Defence, and the Rules of Service of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did this plan envisage the engagement of both the MUP units, the Serbian MUP units, and the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that from the last few words.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that several decisions to establish staff were made in this period, a period of two months, two months and a half?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see two or three decisions in addition to the one dated the 16th of June and the proofing session. This is why I got a little bit mixed up while we were talking about Mr. Djinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when was the final decision to establish the staff issued in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: It was on the 16th of June, 1998, that's the decision that we were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit 4D101 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move, Mr. Lukic, do we have the plan to suppress terrorism in Kosovo -- that -- we don't have it in writing but we have this series of plans. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that we don't have the actual plan, but we have some traces in other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And this meeting -- how many sets of minutes are there for meetings of the inter-departmental staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Only this -- this is the one that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is what I think we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what I don't understand, Mr. Mijatovic, in all of this is why a plan at the instance of the Supreme Defence Council would lead to the non-implementation of a decision made subsequently to establish a MUP staff for Kosovo. I know you said that was the reason, but can you explain how this plan by the VJ could lead to the non-implementation of the establishment of a staff in accordance with the decision of the 16th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think that it is quite simple to understand. The plan that we were talking about envisages that both the MUP forces, MUP units, and the units of the Army of Yugoslavia should engage in those tasks, and it would be logical to have the same units in the same period of time engaged in the same tasks pursuant to two different instruments or documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the one that we looked at earlier establishing the ministerial staff is to do with the command structure of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what decision are you referring to, the 16th of June or an earlier one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, the 16th of June. It deals with the command structure of the MUP, and the MUP needed to have a command structure. So why was it not implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the decision to adopt a plan for anti-terrorist struggle, or rather, to suppress terrorism in Kosovo, it involved both the MUP and the army, was issued before this decision was made on the 9th of June; and the plan followed this decision. So that's why I'm saying that that plan superseded this decision, because it was adopted at a much higher level than that of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And in what way did the plan deal with the command structure of the MUP in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the basic plan that was adopted pursuant to the decision of the state top?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as I said, this plan envisaged the engagement of the police and the Army of Yugoslavia, and planning of anti-terrorist actions on the basis of that plan, that would be to operationalize this plan. So some smaller-scale actions were planned on the basis of this large plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who was to command the MUP in all of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The MUP units in those actions were under command of their officers, such as the PJP detachments, the special anti-terrorist unit; SAJ; the JSO. Of course, if they participated in those actions at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, I have the impression from your earlier answers that prior to the 16th of June there was also a MUP staff for Kosovo. Is that a wrong impression?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the MUP staff for Kosovo and Metohija had been in existence since 1990, and even before that, as early as in 1981 there were police units in Kosovo and Metohija but they were organized on different lines at the federal level, up to 1990. And then in 1990 when the break-up of Yugoslavia actually began, this was the time when all those obligations related to Kosovo and Metohija fell to Serbia, and that is why the first staff was established in 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the result of not implementing the decision of the 16th of June would be to leave in place the existing MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The staff remained there, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the command structure remained as before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not with Gajic because I came and so on, but if you're referring to the personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Lukic, you can perhaps get --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just get it from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Some answers for us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks. [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court Exhibit 4D101.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, could you please read the first paragraph in this document and tell us what kind of a document it is.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The implementation of the second stage of the plan to eliminate terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija provides for the engagement of organs of the Ministry of the Interior, the manoeuvre variant, and the necessary units of the Pristina Corps from the BG, I assume that would be the combat group, in the area. One copy of the plan (the directive and four maps) was delivered to the chief of the first administration of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, Major-General Spasoje Smiljanic on the 15th of July, 1998. You have been briefed on the plan as a whole several times, the last time at the briefing with the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on the 21st of July, 1998, when the order was given to commence the implementation of the plan. So this is a document from the Pristina Corps command sent to the 3rd Army command, the date is the 23rd of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can we conclude on the basis of the first paragraph of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if we read the first paragraph of this document, we can see that the plan was drafted when it was drafted in the first half of July 1998 and that it was adopted and that it could be implemented after the 21st of July. And of course it lists the units that are to be involved in those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this document can we see whether this plan had been approved by someone?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, obviously it had been approved by the then-president. That was on the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move to page 2. I think we're still on page 1 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 3 and could you please read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I do apologise, that's paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read from the second passage beginning with the words: "Operations or activities ..." And could you please read what it says under A.?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: So that's 3 paragraph 3 and then I start with the word "dejstvo," operations. So from A: "The activities in the second stage of the plan are based on the following facts" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read a little bit more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. "That the plan for the engagement of the MUP forces and the Army of Yugoslavia was considered on several occasions and accepted by the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the top leadership of the Army of Yugoslavia and the MUP. While the plan was being considered, the directive and the decision on the map, there were no serious objections to the proposals that were tabled," if that's what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you -- do you know who approved this plan and who was present from the army and the MUP leaders?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as you can see from this first paragraph, this was approved by the then-president of the FRY in the presence of the highest leadership of the Ministry of the Interior and the Army of Yugoslavia, so that would be the Chief of the General Staff and the minister of the interior. They are the highest top-ranking leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And was this plan implemented in practice?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did the deblockade of roads start -- and breaking the strongholds of the KLA through a joint effort of the military and the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the first action started on the 25th of July, 1998, that is when this activity started.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from the MUP of the Republic of Serbia take part in the drafting of this plan, anyone from the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. And I remember that after this plan was adopted our generals, or rather, police generals were - well, how should I put this? - dissatisfied with that because the plan envisaged more forces of the ministry than the ministry actually had available. When I'm talking about forces, I'm talking about level of training, level of equipment, because after all, this is difficult and risky work.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the reason why the plan to combat terrorism was adopted?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was due to the situation at that point in time in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. The terrorist activities were on the rise, the terrorists were practically covering about 50 per cent of the territory. I cannot be very specific on this. I'm saying around 50 per cent of the territory. They jeopardized practically all the major roads leading through Kosovo, all the more important roads leading through Kosovo. They were kidnapping people, stopping them, mistreating them, killing people, wounding people, and so on and so forth. In a word, the safety and security of citizens was jeopardized and their freedom of movement, and I think that was the reason, because there is no other reason why this plan was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the visit paid by Ambassador Holbrooke and what were the consequences of that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I don't know the exact time, but I remember that before that, Mr. Holbrooke was in Kosovo and Metohija in Junik where he had his picture taken with armed members of the so-called KLA, which bolstered them because they thought that this was the support of the US administration. And immediately the ranks increased and as did their armament levels and their terrorist activities. Another situation contributed to that, too, and that is the situation from 1997, the situation in the Republic of Albania, that is to say a neighbouring state, when military barracks were robbed and when masses of weapons were taken from there and a lot of that ended up in Kosovo and Metohija. So in addition to an increase in ranks, there was a higher level of armament on the part of the members of the so-called KLA. And then through their activities, they contributed to this kind of situation in terms of security in Kosovo and Metohija, safety and security, which, in fact, endangered the state itself in that part of the territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just to go back slightly to what you were actually dealing with in this document on the screen, which I appreciate is a VJ document and not a MUP document. It says that during the consideration of the plan there were no serious objections to the proposals and that it was considered and accepted several times by the president and the highest leadership of the army and the MUP. You're saying that that's wrong? Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not present at that meeting, or rather, I did not attend any meetings or did I hear that any of the members of the ministry took part when this plan was drafted. At that meeting that was held in the office of the president of the country when the plan was being adopted, I don't know if anyone objected and if so what the objections were. But I know that police generals were dissatisfied with this plan, as I've already said, because a high level of forces of the Ministry of the Interior was envisaged for participation in this plan and the ministry did not have a sufficient number of trained and equipped personnel for such activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were you one of those dissatisfied with the plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't even a general and I was talking about generals, I do apologise, but on the other hand I didn't see the plan, I've never seen the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who were the generals who were dissatisfied with the plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was General Djordjevic, Stevanovic, Lukic, when they saw what the plan said, what all the units engaged were supposed to be, they were not satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what was done about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The plan was operationalized through specific actions and the units of the Army of Yugoslavia took part in it as well as units of the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I meant what was done to express the dissatisfaction and to have the plan changed so that it was acceptable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot talk about that. I just heard from their conversations that they did not take part in the elaboration of the plan, and that is why that kind of a number of personnel was planned, that the MUP practically didn't have. I really don't know. The plan had already been adopted at the president's -- the president of the republic, and I personally think that after that, there could be no changes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't understand. If you don't have enough men, do you not actually report back to those responsible for the planning that you don't have enough men to implement it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know what number -- I mean, I don't know what the number was of personnel engaged on the basis of that plan. I don't know if they meant the number of overall forces. For example, if these activities are supposed to involve 10.000 policemen and say the MUP had 5, then only those forces could be engaged because the remaining 5 or simply not there, and then later on probably through the planning of activity this was borne in mind and somehow some kind of a compromise was reached there, or rather, those forces that we had available were used in the planning and they could not plan using other forces that we did not have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, I'm reluctant to become involved in extensive questioning of any witness in the course of counsel's examination of that witness, but this witness is making very sweeping statements that when you explore below the surface, he really doesn't seem entirely qualified to make them. So it's important that he, as far as possible, gives us evidence from his own personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, did you ever hear in the MUP staff that the plan for combatting terrorism was submitted to the staff in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never heard of that. I never saw it, and I personally think it was never submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the staff receive any documents from the Army of Yugoslavia in relation to anti-terrorist actions; and if so, in which period?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did, and 1998 [Realtime transcript read in error "NATO"] it wasn't until the end of September, that anti-terrorist activities were carried out and we did receive excerpts from the army, excerpts from maps including axes of activity of the police units that were planned for participation in that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: In 1999, until the order on resubordination was received, these excerpts were received and once this order on resubordination was received, we received excerpts from maps and the textual parts, or rather, the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you something about the role of the staff of the Ministry of the Interior in Kosovo and Metohija. In planning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: A very odd comment in the English transcript in line 23 of page 57. Can someone remind me what was actually said there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It is LiveNote, it was not said in the interpretation. It's a misprint.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I should ask that question again, Your Honour. It's really complicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Perhaps the interpreter can give us the answer again from recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Unfortunately not, the witness would have to repeat exactly what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think you should clarify that, Mr. Lukic. It doesn't make any sense, that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll have to repeat. I'll have to repeat the question, you'll have to repeat the answer. The MUP staff in Kosovo, did they receive from the Army of Yugoslavia some documents related to anti-terrorist actions? And I think that we were talking about 1998.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I said that in 1998 for every anti-terrorist action that had been planned, the staff received excerpts from maps where there were markings or we received photocopies. That is to say, forces that were taking part in the actions, or rather, police units that were taking part in these actions. The staff would send this to the units that were planned to carry out these actions so that they would action in accordance with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the beginning of 1999 until the decision on subordination, what did the staff receive?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: From the moment when the bombing started, when the war started, that is, until the order on subordination was received - I'm using the term "subordination" because that's what the law says - a period had already elapsed in wartime until this order was not adopted. So we did what we did in 1998, we received excerpts. And after the order on subordination was received, in addition to these excerpts from maps, we got the textual part of tasks in the form of orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it is all right now. I've moved on to another topic and I said that I would ask you about the role of the MUP staff in planning anti-terrorist actions. What did the role of the staff consist of then in the planning of specific anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: For the most part, the role of the staff was to submit to the Pristina Corps elements, or rather, data about MUP units in the area that could have been planned for this particular activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the first anti-terrorist action was carried out, was a joint meeting held between the officers of the Army of Yugoslavia and the officers of the MUP and do you remember roughly when this happened, if so, if such a meeting did take place at all?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I cannot remember the exact date. Perhaps it was two or three days before this first action started, a meeting was held of all the officers of both the army and the police, I'm referring to commanders of units, that is, in order to familiarize them with the general guide-lines from the adopted plan on combatting terrorism in order for them to be introduced to the elements of this first task and so that people who did not know one another and who were supposed to act in the same area would meet, that is to say officers of the army and officers of the police were present at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you just be a bit more specific. You said a few days before the first action. Can you give us the month and year?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: It was the month of July, say between the 21st and the 25th. Now, I cannot say whether it was the 22nd or the 23rd of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I've already said, officers of the Army of Yugoslavia and of the police, and I think that the chiefs of the secretariats were there, too, but I'm not sure about that. I cannot remember. However, commanders of units of the army and of the police who were active in the area and of course the representatives of the staff and of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did any civilians attend the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no, and there was no need for any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where was this meeting held?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: This meeting was held in a meeting room at the SUP building in Pristina. This was a meeting room and it was big enough to accommodate all these attendees, there were quite a few there. There was no other area that would be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for this first anti-terrorist action, were there several such joint meetings?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember them. I don't think there were any, except for this first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you about reporting of PJPs to the staff. What about the commanders of detachments? And when I'm saying "you," I mean the MUP staff. Did they, the commanders of the PJP detachments, did they submit reports to you after the actions were completed?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No. The commanders of the special police units did not submit any reports to the staff; however, they were duty-bound, like any authorised officials, because all of this consisted of authorised officers, so like any other authorised officers, after such activities, if there were any elements on account of which the territorial secretariats would have to take action, they were duty-bound to report to them so they could take action, for example, carry out an investigation, put out a fire, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now that we're dealing with this issue I'd like to ask you this. Can you tell us something more about what it is that the PJP units were supposed to inform the SUPs, what were those events that were of interest from a security point of view that they were supposed to report on?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: For example, if any corpses were found or any crimes committed, if there were any fires, as I have said, if it involved civilians, if the civilians were on the move and they needed accommodation, if they needed accommodation, food, water, if civilians needed any kind of assistance, if anything concerned the life of people in that territory and anything that fell under the jurisdiction of the secretariat according to the law, they were supposed to inform on all of these matters because secretariats, according to the legislation, acted on their own without waiting for instructions. Not just secretariats, but any other authorised official had the duty to act in accordance with the regulations. This is why they were authorised officials. They did not have to wait for somebody to order them to do something. And in order for the secretariat to take action, they had to have information, they had to have knowledge about what had happened. In that context if members of PJP units had any information, then, yes, they had duty to inform the secretariat in order for the secretariat to take action accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the MUP staff exert any influence over the course of any anti-terrorist action?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The MUP staff did not exert any influence nor could it affect course of anti-terrorist activities because the units acted on the basis of a plan that had been prepared for a particular action, and officers who were in charge of those units were responsible for implementation of the plan. Activities were carried out in the field, the units were controlled by radio equipment that the MUP staff could not monitor because we used different frequencies. So the MUP staff could not follow the course of any action or affect it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know how and in what way commanders of PJP units informed about the course of anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know this. I was not out in the field, I did not take part in any action, and I don't know how that transpired, who was informed, how that unfolded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you going as far as to say that the MUP for these anti-actions took orders from the VJ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The police units which participated in specific anti-terrorist actions received documents from the army, which means that the MUP staff did not draft a single map, a single order, a single task relating to these anti-terrorist activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could answer my question. Are you saying that the MUP units involved took orders from the VJ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the ground, each officer was in charge of his own units in those actions. Now, as to whether somebody combined this from some post, whether there was an officer who was in charge of both units, I don't know, I wasn't out on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to clarify something, Mr. Mijatovic. Was it policemen who commanded police units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Detachment commanders commanded their detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the 28th of March, rather, the night between the 28th and 29th of March, 1999, when the SUP Pristina building was hit, were there any technical capabilities for anyone to contact you via radio equipment from the ground, from the field? When I say "you," I'm referring to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understood that. When the building of the secretariat of the interior in Pristina was hit, the antenna system and relay system were destroyed. I'm not a technical person and I don't know much about this, but the equipment that is used for sending out signals was destroyed, so practically we were cut off from the people who were on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You made a gesture with your hand. Where were those antennas located?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: They were on the building of the Pristina SUP, which had been bombed, and this is how these antenna systems came to be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the decision was issued, the plan for anti-terrorist combat which was in July of 1998, did any of the MUP seniors come to Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Generals Vlastimir Djordjevic and Obrad Stevanovic came. They held a meeting at the staff and they informed senior officers about that and that we needed to participate in those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that they informed about that, what did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These two senior officers of the MUP, how long did they stay there in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: They stayed until the end of September throughout the time that anti-terrorist activities were carried out, but I couldn't claim to you with certainty that both of them were present all the time. But in principle, one of them would be present because they had to go and visit their families and maybe they had to go for other reasons to Belgrade, but in principle one of them was always present down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about 1999, what was the situation like then regarding these two generals?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in 1999 too, but I think that General Obrad Stevanovic spent more time there than General Djordjevic, but both of them were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the two of them frequently go out in the field?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: They did go out in the field, but who they went to see, what were their tasks, what were their intentions, I don't know. I never asked them that and they never told me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic come to Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the minister came as well. I wouldn't be able to say how many times he came, but he did come and I think that whenever he came he invariably held meetings with police officers, senior officers in Kosovo and Metohija, he would provide his assessments, guide-lines. I wouldn't be able to give you any more details, but I'm sure that there are minutes from those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's quite enough at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you not meet him when he came to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I told you that meetings were held with senior officers, and naturally members of the staff were present there as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And did that include you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was present. I wouldn't be able to claim that I attended every single meeting, but I did attend them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to turn to a different matter, Mr. Mijatovic, I would like to ask you something about the relationship between the MUP staff and organizational units in Kosovo, that is to say secretariats of the interior, departments of interior, and police stations. Could you now briefly describe to us some of the tasks performed by the secretariats of the interior in general, including those in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The competencies of the secretariats of the interior as territorial units of the Ministry of the Interior were identical, regardless of whether they were located in Kosovo and Metohija or in some other part of Serbia. They carried out tasks and assignments in their territory aimed at suppressing crime, control and regulation of traffic, maintaining law and order, putting out fires, since they had fire units in their composition. They also carried out some administrative work for the needs of the citizens. They issued IDs, driving licences, licence plates, and so on, also passports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the secretariats of the interior have any plans based on which they worked?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Each organizational unit of the Ministry of the Interior drafts its own plans in order to organize the work and assignments and tasks from their competencies. This is something that is done at the level of the Ministry of the Interior, that is to say at the highest level there are yearly plans produced as well as monthly plans and the secretariats did this for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you -- ask you this: Did the staff --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again you're being asked to repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat my question, Mr. Mijatovic. I probably spoke too fast. Did the staff adopt work-plans for the secretariats of the interior or for departments of the interior or for police stations in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, it did not. The staff couldn't do that. There was no grounds for the staff to do that. As I told you, secretariats drafted these plans on their own, chief of the secretariat followed the implementation of the plans with his associates. He would take measures if the plan was not properly implemented, and ultimately the chief of the secretariat was responsible to the minister of the interior for the work of his secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the staff control and approve the plans for regular work tasks adopted by the MUP organizational units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No. The staff did not receive those plans at all, nor did the staff have any knowledge of those plans or implement their, or rather, control their implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the MUP staff in any way control and direct the work of the organizational units in Kosovo and Metohija, the MUP organizational units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. This was done by the officers who headed those organizational units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who directed the work of the border police posts?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The posts of the border police were, territorially speaking, located in the Republic of Serbia, not only in Kosovo but in other areas as well, that is to say not only in Kosovo and Vojvodina, but also in the central part of Serbia. And territorially they were within the territory covered by the secretariat. However, in the organizational sense they were directly linked to the administration of the border police which was located in the seat of the Ministry of the Interior, and for their work they were responsible and they received orders from the chief of their administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit 6D266 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have the document in front of you, Mr. Mijatovic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So could we begin right away. Could you tell us who sent this document and who are the addressees?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: This document was sent by the chief of the public security department, General Djordjevic. The date is the 1st of July, 1998, and the addressees are a certain number of secretariats, the ministry staff in Pristina, the border police stations, not all of them, but just those which are located in Kosovo and Metohija and in Presevo and in Prohor Pcinjski, so this is outside the territory of Kosovo and Metohija in the central part of Serbia, the police administration at the MUP headquarters in Belgrade, the crime police administration, the traffic police administration, the border police administration, and the operations centre at the seat or headquarters of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And does this document actually contains orders for their work, are they being ordered what to do?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these are the orders for work since this was the period and the time when weapons were being smuggled and ammunition was being smuggled into the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and the efforts -- efforts were being made to prevent that, so the orders were to that effect. The secretariats or the police personnel in the field were supposed to do that even without receiving specific orders, but this was yet another order to increase their effectiveness in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, but I have to interrupt this direct examination to clarify one thing, and I think that interpreters have to help us. Every time when we hear word "nalog" which is something different from "naredjenje" we are getting the same translation, order, and I think that we should have a distinction in between these two terms, because "nalog" is something what's specific for MUP and "naredjenje" is something more specific for the army. And I don't know right now -- because now I have confusion with the testimony of Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you indicate what the distinction is?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The distinction is the consequence of the mode of work these two institutions, military works, strictly based on orders; police works based on the law, laws and sublaws. So here we have something -- we have orders in the police sometimes as well, different kinds, and we would be dealing with that during our case, but we have to have distinction in between "order" and this other term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The witness in relation to this document is saying that it includes orders to prevent the importation of weapons, something that the police would do automatically, but this was to reinforce that duty. Now, would you say it wasn't an order to that effect?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What would you say it was?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English I really -- I'm not sure that I know the exact term. That's why I'm addressing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're likely to be leading a witness who bears to be an expert in the affairs of the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but we'll have the whole mess by that time in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It can't be cured at the end of the case. Could be maybe direction or instruction; more direction, I think. Instructions we have separate instructions, but direction would be more line like the meaning of this term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Probably still comes to: You'll do as you're told.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it's different from an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, we will seek some guide --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, definitely it's binding. I'm not telling that the other category is not binding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will seek guidance from CLSS and I shall let you know if there is any way of dealing with this other than to hear submissions in due course, but it will probably be tomorrow before I can tell you. I think you should proceed on the basis that you've alerted us to it and we will take steps to ensure that there is no prejudice caused to you by the interpretation of these words in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I think it's a good time for our break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. We have to break at this stage again, Mr. Mijatovic, that will be for an hour for lunch. Could you again leave the courtroom, please, with the usher and we will see you again at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.48 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, you've worn one of our number down. It would be obvious to anyone observing here this morning that Judge Kamenova was unwell and she's really not able to continue this afternoon. Hopefully she will be back tomorrow, but we will meanwhile continue in her absence since we consider that it is in the interests of justice to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I should also record that I believe you had a discussion with the interpreters at the lunch break. Did you work out a solution?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the interpreters suggested that we should use the other order with Serbian word in brackets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The Mr. Ivetic approach to difficulties of translation. I think that's a reasonable course to follow, and you've placed on record earlier today the reason for doing that, so we will be particularly alert to any problem that may emerge from this when we come to look at all the evidence. Would you please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, can we continue? Mr. Mijatovic, can we continue?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please don't fall asleep on me now.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we're now talking about the relationship between the MUP staff and the MUP organizational units in Kosovo and Metohija and we're looking at 6D266, Exhibit 6D266. I would just like to ask you a couple of brief questions. Can we see from this document that the border police stations are receiving separate reports separate from the secretariats of the interior in whose territory they are actually situated?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is quite obvious. This telegram is addressed to the border police stations in addition to the secretariats in the same territory, which shows that the border police stations are not operating within the secretariat. On the other hand, this document is also sent to the border police administration so that it can be kept in the loop as to the tasks that its stations have received because this is sent from -- this is sent by the sector chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who issued orders, "nalog," to the secretariats of the interior in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The secretariats, not only in Kosovo and Metohija, but throughout Serbia, received their orders from the Ministry of the Interior and from the administrators of the departmental units, I mean the administration for the traffic police, the administration for the general police service, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The chain of issuing orders, "nalogs," and the reporting chain from the Ministry of the Interior and secretariat of the interior linking the two, did it remain unchanged regardless of the existence of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, or rather, no. This chain of management was not changed for a very simple reason. The staff was not an organizational unit of the ministry, and the existence of the staff did not disrupt this chain of management. So the staff is not an organizational unit, and as such it is not superior to or subordinate to any other unit except for the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, 6D266 is one of the documents talking about that but also some other documents, 6D129, 6D1352, 6D1353, and that would be enough for now. The orders, "nalogs," that the administrations in the seat of the ministry issued to the secretariats of the interior in Kosovo and Metohija, were they at the same time sent to the staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The MUP staff did receive those too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why was the MUP staff informed at the same time as these other units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already explained, the orders, "nalogs," went straight to the secretariats and they had to comply with those orders regardless of what the staff had to say, and they were sent to the staff in order to keep the staff in the loop, to keep it informed. And any assistance needed to be rendered -- but the secretariats acted -- they bypassed the staff in their operation. The staff could not change the order in any way, the "naredba," order, it could not be changed in any way by the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And whose orders, "nalogs," were executed by lower-level units such as the departments of the interior and the police stations?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: They carried out the orders, "nalogs," of the secretariat headed by the secretariat chief. And as a rule, the ministry did not issue direct orders to the OUPs and the stations, but it sent them to the secretariats and they relay them to those lower-level units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when regular tasks are carried out, how is management or control exercised, this line along which the orders, or "nalogs," are being handed down?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as you can see from what I told you, it is a vertical line, from the ministry to the secretariat, from the secretariat to the OUP, and down to the police station, and from the MUP to the staff. The staff could, possibly on the orders of somebody from the ministry to relay some order, "nalog," to the secretariats, or possibly it may have updated some task or some obligation. When I say "update," let me clarify this term. Unlike in the military where tasks are carried out on the orders, "naredjenje," a soldier waits for an order, "naredjenje," to carry out his task. A police officer is an authorised official who has the power and the obligation to carry out certain actions under the law. He does not have to wait, he must not wait for the order to do something. He must do whatever is necessary under the law. When I said that the staff could update some obligations, what I meant was that the staff could remind the secretariat in question if note was taken of the fact that some things were not done as they should have been done, the staff could remind the secretariat to increase, to step up its activities or to carry out its duties if the secretariat was duty-bound to do it. But it could not take any decisions on its own initiative and it could not issue any orders, "nalog," because it was not superior to the secretariat. It could propose, suggest, recommend.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that the staff could not issue any orders, "nalog," to the secretariats. And let me now ask you whether the MUP staff or its chief or head could organize the work of the secretariats of the interior?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I think that we've already said that, no, it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did MUP staff or its head, could they deal with any personnel issues in the secretariats who would be appointed and who would be removed from office in the secretariat or other organizational units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, it did not have any powers to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the MUP staff or its head -- or was it able to impose any sanctions for the failure on the part of the secretariats of the interior or lower-level organizational units to carry out their tasks?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, it did not have those powers. The chief of the secretariat had this kind of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The MUP staff or its head, were they responsible to the minister for the work of the secretariats of the interior?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No. It could not plan, it could not organize, it could not manage the work of the secretariats, it could not control whether they're doing their work properly, so it could not be responsible for their work to the minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you gave us a series of documents there related to 6D266, one of them was 6D1353, is that number correct, because it seems to be a document dealing with the repatriation of German citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's obviously my mistake, Your Honours, so we should strike that document from the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, you've explained to us what couldn't be done, yet in practice did it happen that the MUP staff or its head did take some measures related to the planning, organization, or management of the organizational units of the MUP in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, never, as far as I know, and he was not in a position to do so because the regulations for the functioning of the ministry simply did not allow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The MUP staff or its head, did they have any authority in terms of rewards, assignment, dismissal in terms of member of units in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Again my answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What would the line of orders, "nalogs," be like if the organs of the Ministry of the Interior were to receive their orders?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: It would be like what the secretariats do. As I said, the MUP order the secretariats, the secretariats order their OUPs and police stations. Had that chain been disrupted or placed in a different way, then the MUP as I've already said, they would not directly give orders to the OUPs or police stations, they would not be giving orders to the secretariats either, I'm trying to speak a little slower for interpretation, they would give order, "nalog," to the staff, then the staff to the secretariats and the secretariats to their OUPs and police stations. So there wouldn't be a double chain, there would just be one chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe you've already answered, but because of my own line of questioning I'll ask you again. The MUP staff, was it an organizational unit of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, and it cannot be because the rules do not envisage that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What organizational units does the MUP have?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: They're organizational units of the ministry within every sector, I can talk about the public security sector. Within the public security sector in the seat of the ministry there are so-called internal organizational units that are within the seat of the ministry itself. Every organizational unit has a certain line of work, for example --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, what are the names of these organizational units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to say but I don't want to encumber the interpreters too much. They are called --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The transcript is frozen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The witness has stopped speaking as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stopped because Mr. Lukic signalled to me that I should stop. It was my impression that there was something wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We stopped at the question of organizational units within the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've already said that within the seat of the ministry there are the so-called internal organizational units, and every one of them manages a particular line of work. For instance -- oh, yes, and for the most part, those are administrations. For instance, the police administration, the traffic police administration, the crime police -- the crime investigation police administration, the administration for analytical affairs, the computer science administration, the communications administration, the joint services administration, and so on, not to go into all of that, and then also there is the duty operations centre. That is what has to do with the seat of the ministry itself. Earlier on I spoke about the fact that secretariats are territorial organizational units of the Ministry of the Interior covering certain parts of a particular territory. According to the same principle, a secretariat has those lines of work too. They are either departments or divisions. So the situation is the same as I said within the seat of the ministry. Again, there is the traffic police, crime investigation, analytical affairs, joint services, I cannot remember exactly, IT, and so on and so forth. So it is what I said about the ministry itself, too, the seat of the ministry, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija, what kind of a body is that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, the staff does not belong to the group that I mentioned a while ago, it's not an organizational unit. The staff was a temporary, an auxiliary, body of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The indictment charges that the MUP staff is a small-scale ministry, or it was either in the Prosecutor's pre-trial brief, I can't say exactly right now. Before the changes, before the provincial SUP was abolished, how big was the staff of the provincial SUP in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I don't even know how many people were employed at the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Roughly?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it involved many, many more people than the staff did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tens? Hundreds of people?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm waiting for the interpretation to finish. As we could see, the staff involved about ten people as members. I take the liberty of saying that the provincial SUP must have had several hundred employees, perhaps even a thousand. You should take this with a grain of salt, but it is certain that it was many times more than the member -- the number of members of staff -- the number of members of staff of the MUP staff of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What pertains to the decision -- what could it do in relation to decisions made by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please call up in e-court Exhibit 6D690.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think I've missed something in this, Mr. Lukic, which you can maybe remind me of. We've just had a reference to the provincial SUP. Have we had that referred to already?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Lukic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, today in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So how does that fit into this structure or is that coming?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We just -- I just wanted to show the number of people working in one or another organ that we exactly wanted to show that there is no comparison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I cannot see you because of this pole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your good fortune again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, we see in front of us this document. Could you tell us what kind of a document this is and who is sending it and who is it being sent to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: We're talking about 6D690?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document that the staff of the Ministry of the Interior in Pristina sent and I signed it on behalf of General Lukic probably because at that moment he was not there or he was busy with other things, I don't think it really matters right now. It has to do with sending the agreement that the FRY signed with the OSCE mission, or rather, with the OSCE in relation to the establishment of a verification mission in Kosovo and Metohija. It was sent so that the secretariats could initially familiarise themselves with the agreement, and also they should learn what should be done in this connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this document and on many others that were sent by the MUP staff, we see that it says in the number 12A number 223-83. We would be interested in the part where it says 12A. Did an organizational unit of the MUP have a letter by way of designation in addition to a number in order to show its affiliation, or was this A characteristic of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Every internal organizational unit of the Ministry of the Interior in the seat, that is to say in Belgrade, had its own initial number for the documents that it sent out, and on that basis one could tell inter alia whose document this was. In this case number 12 belonged to the police administration at the seat of the ministry. Since the staff in Pristina, the MUP staff in Pristina, did not have its own number in terms of this initial number, this registration number, it was assigned this number and that's why this A was added in order to make a distinction, to know that these were documents from the staff. Because that also says that the MUP staff in Pristina was not an organizational unit of the ministry according to the Rules on Organization.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which entity in the ministry would normally have dealt with this? Is police administration the name of that section?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The police administration had this number and they used it for their own documents that they sent. Now, who decided on the actual numbers, believe me, I don't know, and on the basis of what regulation. There is probably a regulation to that effect, but I assume that other services dealt with that. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not what I was asking you. I was asking you under which department in headquarters in Belgrade the subject of the verification mission fell.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you've told us that the MUP staff has no organizational role in the command structure. So along comes a new development and the introduction of the KVM, and this memo here is telling the SUPs about that. Now, who or which -- which department of the MUP in Belgrade would normally have dealt with this in the absence of the MUP staff for Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I've understood the question. As for the text of the agreement, we got that from the leadership of the ministry and I assume that it was the minister's office or cabinet because I cannot remember exactly who it was that sent this document to us, giving us the task to send it further on to the secretariats so that they would be made aware of it and that they would act accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, I'm still struggling, as I'm sure you realize, to understand where this MUP staff fits in and what the point of having it at all is if it's got no organizational role within the system. I'm trying to understand why this document should be issued by the MUP staff for Kosovo and should not come from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean why this went through the staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is not the first case that orders, "nalog," for issued through the staff -- well, there would be a problem, for instance, and General Lukic would talk to the minister or I would talk to some of the top people over there, we would present the problem, and they would, for instance, say do this and that, send a document to the secretariats so that they should act in such and such a way. The staff would do that then on behalf of the leadership of the ministry. That is what was done in this case because -- because the ministry did not send this directly to the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rather -- yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That means, surely, that there must be a document from the ministry sending it to the MUP staff for Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably, probably there was, but I cannot remember that and I don't have anything like that here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I -- I beg your pardon, may I just add one more thing? One should not rule out the possibility that somebody brought that there without an accompanying letter, the text of the agreement, brought it to the staff with the task of the staff being to send this further on to the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: My worry at the moment, Mr. Mijatovic, is that the MUP staff for Kosovo is a body with a very fuzzy shape that I'm trying to focus more clearly in my mind's eye, and at the moment I just don't see where it fits in, unfortunately. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hope we are getting there, Your Honour. I think that Mr. Mijatovic by the end of his testimony will be able to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, I shall be patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, what were the names of the top people in MUP in organizational units? What were the typical names? What was the name of the first person within the police or within the secretariat of the interior?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand your question. Those are chiefs, chief of the criminal investigation, police, chief of the secretariat, and so on, so as not to list all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that the name of the first person in the staff, the title of the first person in the staff is different and we use the term "head of the staff." What can we conclude based on that, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The head of the staff, the title itself, indicates that this person heads a staff, not secretariats, but a staff because if the head of staff also headed secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija then perhaps that person would be known as head of police in Kosovo and Metohija or head of organizational units of the ministry in Kosovo and Metohija or something similar to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you describe the process of reporting within the Ministry of the Interior, how did that function?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The reporting functioned in the following way. First of all, let me say that the reporting was done on the basis of the instructions on reporting that were in power for the entire Ministry of the Interior, and reporting or informing followed an opposite path then, command and control. The police stations and departments of the interior within their territories informed the secretariats, and then secretariats in turn informed the Ministry of the Interior directly. In parallel, reports were also sent by them to the staff in Pristina. Based on those reports coming from the secretariat, the analytical officer within the staff would produce a resume of all these reports coming from the entire territory of Kosovo and Metohija and draft a single report which the staff would then send to the Ministry of the Interior in order to have a better survey of what was going on because all of these -- all of these pieces of information pertained to certain categories, either traffic accidents or crimes and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see in e-court 6D1323.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document hasn't been translated, as we can see in e-court, so I would kindly ask you, Mr. Mijatovic, to tell us what type of a document this is.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: This is the document I just mentioned, and it pertains to a reporting within the Ministry of the Interior. It is known as instruction on informing and reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it on the basis of this document that reporting was done in the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you remember, what kind of reports are made pursuant to this instruction? What kind of reports SUPs produce?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I understood your question. I was just waiting for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. May I inquire when we might expect a translation of this because if we're going to go into detail with him about the contents of this document, I need an English translation to cross-examine with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We had a prioritize our documents sent for the translation, and I think that this one is scheduled to be translated with our expert witness. So I will not -- I don't have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We can deal with it then with the expert --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but I'll just ask Mr. Mijatovic about his knowledge. I'm not going to use this document. I just wanted to draw the attention of Your Honours to be aware of the existence of such a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Proceed without the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell us without referring to this document, to the instruction, what do you know, what kind of reports exist within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: There are so-called daily reports, daily reporting, meaning that reports are sent on a daily basis. Then there is a so-called urgent reporting, depending on the events. And then there is also occasional reporting or a reporting done in a certain period of time. When I say this, I'm referring to monthly and yearly reports that secretariats are duty-bound to send to the senior officials of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when was this duty introduced for the secretariats of the interior to send daily and special reports to the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These special reports have to do with urgent reporting or some events of significance that needed to be reported on in a special way. As for the duty of the staff, or rather, the duty of the secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija to report to the staff, this was introduced in 1990 when the first staff was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were the secretariats of the interior duty-bound to send periodic reports to the staff in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, they did not have such duty and the staff did not receive monthly or yearly reports on the work of secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who did the secretariats of the interior send daily and urgent reports to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: As I have told you, they sent daily reports both to the ministry and to the staff in parallel, as well as urgent reports whenever there was an event that required urgent reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "in parallel," you mean simultaneously?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, simultaneously, it's an identical report, an identical report is sent to the ministry and to the staff. There was no difference in the content there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did these reports sent by the secretariat of ministry go to the staff and, or rather, how were they sent to the staff before the bombing started and afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Before the bombing started, these reports were mostly sent via communications equipment, that is to say by fax or by dispatch; and later on when NATO bombing started, when these lines were disrupted, the only way to send daily reports was by courier. Naturally, depending on the events, sometimes we were unable to receive daily reports from all secretariats, but whenever couriers managed to come in they would bring all the reports for all the preceding days. So sometimes we did not have information about something that happened in the preceding period of time because sometimes these reports by secretariats were our only source of information about some events.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The reports sent by the staff to the ministry seat in Belgrade were signed by whom?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: These reports were mostly signed by General Lukic; if he was absent, I would sign them; and if I wasn't present either, then some other members of the staff would sign it, whoever was present when the analytics officer completed the report. There was no need for them to wait for one of us to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How would you describe the reports you received from SUPs in terms of their clarity and comprehensibility?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the analyst would receive these reports and he would review them. Sometimes they would reach me, but the analytical never complained to me that he did not understand the reports or was unable to review them because something was not clear. So I think that everything was fine in these reports and there was no need for us to intervene in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
